title: I Printed the Open-Plan Meeting That Wasn't About Budget

parts.text: I was updating a ticket when I heard my name through the cheap partition like I was already gone. Our open-plan office has no secrets, only volume. I am thirty-five, mid-level manager who hates being a manager. Two directors, Hal and Sasha, were "budgeting" at the collab table eight feet away. Hal said, "Move Dev's projects off him before the announcement." Sasha said, "He's the reason we can restructure quietly." I am Dev. I kept typing so the keyboard would sound normal. My coffee had gone film-on-top cold, that skin that makes you gag if you forget. I opened a dummy spreadsheet. Hal laughed. "He'll think it's a promotion track." Sasha lowered her voice and failed. "Don't put anything in email. Use the hallway." They were in no hallway. A junior named Mei looked at me, eyes wide, because she had heard it too. I messaged her: stay quiet, write what you heard. I wrote what I heard. Then I noticed Hal's laptop faced me, auto-captioning their Teams recording of the "budget sync." They had recorded themselves. The captions said my name, restructure, don't email. "How long have you been sitting there?" he said, suddenly friendly. I said, "The whole meeting you didn't invite me to." Sasha tried a joke about acoustics. "Let's take this to a room." I stood too. "That's company property if it's our captions." It was my personal phone. I stepped back. The captions were still glowing through his laptop vent like a guilty nightlight.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: He is reaching for my phone while their own Teams captions still name me as the quiet restructure.

social.video_title: They auto-captioned my layoff in the open — Part 1/2
social.description: Eight feet of partition, a cold coffee skin, and Teams captions that did not know how to whisper. A junior was already taking notes. Would you have photographed the laptop?

parts.text: I did not give him the phone. I said, "If captions are company property, so is the recording." I emailed myself the photo from the hallway they had recommended, which was funny in a dead way. HR's after-hours ticket form sent an auto-reply with a ticket number that sounded like a lottery. Monday, legal had the Teams file. Hal called it a hypothetical. The captions were not hypothetical. Sasha tried to say I had eavesdropped. Mei submitted her notes with timestamps. The HVAC roar was even on the recording, a stupid mundane alibi for nobody. They paused the restructure. They did not make me director of anything. They offered a retention bonus that felt like hush money. I took career counseling instead and a written statement that my projects would not be quietly moved. Hal was "aligned to a regional role." Sasha still says hello in the kitchen like we share a joke. We do not. I take calls in a booked room now. I also bought a mug that says nothing, on purpose. Mei got a mentorship that is actually on a calendar. Months later a recruiter asked why I left middle management energy on the table. I told him about auto-captions. He hired me. I still flinch when HVAC kicks on. That is not trauma theater. That is just a building doing what buildings do, and my brain doing what brains do after they hear their own name used as a budget line.

social.video_title: Legal played the Teams file back — Part 2/2
social.description: Hypotheticals do not auto-caption. I skipped the hush bonus and took the written statement. Have you ever heard your name through a partition?
